feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Dems demand DHS fund election security. And, journalist Gloria Steinem has died
entry.summary: Two Democrats are demanding that Homeland Security officials fund election security ahead of the midterms. And, trail-blazing journalist Gloria Steinem has died.

entry.title: Families of the missing in Nepal's flash floods perform symbolic cremations
entry.summary: Eight days after Nepal's flash floods, families who can't find loved ones perform symbolic cremations.

entry.title: China's Xi visits Egypt for the first time in a decade
entry.summary: Xi Jinping's visit to Egypt for the first time in a decade, and during the Iran war, comes as U.S. allies broaden their security ties.

entry.title: Critics question legality of Venezuela oil deals
entry.summary: Chevron's $7 billion Venezuela bet deepens U.S. ties to the country's oil industry. Critics say the deal poses risks to democracy and could fuel discontent over Washington's embrace of the government.

entry.title: U.S.-Israel relations are on the rocks ahead of elections
entry.summary: Relations between the Trump administration and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have turned rocky since Trump called a truce with Iran. Trump seeks progress in Gaza, but Netanyahu is taking a defiant stance ahead of an election.

entry.title: Xi visits Egypt as China seeks deeper influence across the Mideast
entry.summary: China's President Xi Jinping visits Egypt this week for the first time in a decade. The trip illustrates China's growing ambitions at a time when U.S. influence has been weakened by its war in Iran.

entry.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
entry.summary: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have asked a judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country

entry.title: A jury in Malta acquits a businessman in the killing of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia
entry.summary: Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia had written extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles in Malta. She was killed by a car bomb in 2017, at age 53.

entry.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
entry.summary: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

entry.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
entry.summary: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.
